title: Trump's 'no new wars' pledge vs. Iran-Israel exchange
narrative:
On June 8, 2026, Iran and Israel exchanged direct fire for the first time since the April truce. Iran launched ~30 ballistic missiles at Israel in retaliation for an Israeli strike on Beirut's Dahiyeh suburb (a Hezbollah-linked building). Israel responded with two waves of airstrikes on Iran, including Tehran and the Mahshahr petrochemical complex. Both sides announced a halt to strikes by Monday afternoon. US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social demanding they 'immediately stop shooting.' White House says Trump called Netanyahu to discuss the crisis.

Separately, Trump walked out of an NBC 'Meet the Press' interview when pressed on election fraud claims. He also told NBC he 'never promised not to start a new war' — contradicting his signature 'no new wars' campaign pledge. The US-Israeli war on Iran began February 28, 2026 with a joint US-Israel attack — a war Trump launched.
telemetry: Trump's 'no new wars' was a core 2024 campaign promise, repeated at dozens of rallies. CNN fact-check documented the contradiction.

Trump told the Financial Times: 'I call the shots... he [Netanyahu] doesn't call the shots' — yet Israel struck Beirut despite US assurances it wouldn't, and Netanyahu proceeded with strikes on Iran after Trump reportedly told him not to escalate.
The US began this war on Feb 28 with a joint attack on Iran. The 'truce' in April was fragile from the start — US continued naval blockade, Israel continued occupying southern Lebanon.
Iranian missiles targeted Israeli military airbases (Ramat David, Tel Nof, Nevatim); Israel targeted civilian petrochemical infrastructure (Karun plant in Mahshahr).
Oil prices rallied on the strikes (per WSJ: 'Oil Rallies After Iran-Israel Trade Strikes').

BBC Persian editor analysis: Iran's strike 'suggests the regime's sense of resilience is growing' — they acted after an attack on an ally (Hezbollah), not on their own territory, signaling a doctrinal shift from 'strategic patience' to 'offensive deterrence.'
analysis:
— How Trump's War on Iran Buried His 'No New Wars' Promise
Angle: The contradiction is not just between Trump's campaign rhetoric and the war he started — it's between his public de-escalation theater ('stop shooting!') and the reality that the war he launched continues to escalate beyond his control. Netanyahu defies him. Iran shifts doctrine. Markets tremble. The 'peace negotiator' is the arsonist.
